sections.title: Two-person crew timing tower check
sections.what: Runs one multi-user browser flow that creates a crew, has a friend join, locks calls for both, and checks the timing tower display and accessibility.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the comment about the week's first join. The flow tests ranking with two real people.
sections.watch_out: The invite code is read directly from the database, so this test fails if the database cannot be reached.

summary: A browser test with two people in one crew: they each lock calls, and the owner checks the timing tower ranks them correctly with form, scores and a provisional label.
purpose: Protects the crew timing tower: ranking, call counts, form icons, scores, position changes and accessibility.
why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond a comment that everyone joined this week, so no one has changed places.
how: Creates an owner and a friend. The owner creates a crew through the API and the test reads its invite code from the database. The friend joins in a second browser context and locks two good calls. The owner locks one poor call. The owner opens the timing tower, checks the friend is rank 1 with two calls and good form, checks the owner's poor form, checks Brier score and Read Rating labels, checks no position changes, checks the provisional label, and runs an accessibility scan.
inputs: A running app and database with sample moments.
risks: The test reads the invite code straight from the database, so it needs database access. Score labels use number patterns, so a change in format breaks it.
debug: If the row order is wrong, check the saved calls and the grades. If the database step fails, check the database connection and the crew record.
